Settings: sklearn silhouette_score, Euclidean, on the same scaled space; exact up to 20,000 customers, 10,000-point subsample above (rfm_scoring.py)

Measures: mean over clusters of the worst within-to-between scatter ratio
between-cluster over within-cluster dispersion, scaled by df
log W_k against its expectation under a structureless reference
Null_comparison: YES - this is the null correction
Settings: B = GAP_B = 50 reference datasets per K; reference drawn uniformly over a box ALIGNED TO THE DATA'S PRINCIPAL AXES (the paper's recommended variant, not a bounding box in the raw axes); s_k = sd(ref) * sqrt(1 + 1/B); rule: the smallest k with Gap(k) >= Gap(k+1) - s_(k+1); K range 2..10 plus the k=1 baseline, so K=1 is a possible answer and is reported when it wins

Measures: minimum single-linkage separation divided by the maximum cluster diameter
Settings: Euclidean on the full pairwise distance matrix of the same scaled space; separation = min over cluster pairs of the closest pair of points; diameter = max over clusters of the farthest pair. Worst-case geometry, not average

Measures: worst cluster's co-assignment rate between halves
Null_comparison: implicitly - it asks whether structure replicates
Settings: reps = PS_REPS = 20 random 50/50 splits; the training half is clustered and its centroids assign the test half, the test half is clustered on its own, and the score is the worst cluster's within-cluster pair co-assignment rate, averaged over splits; threshold PS_THRESHOLD = 0.80. The threshold is a convention, so ksel_ps_thresholds.csv reports 0.70/0.80/0.85/0.90 as well

Measures: mean ARI between a refit on a resample and the reference labels
Settings: BOOT_N = 100 resamples with replacement; the model is refitted on each resample and used to predict ALL customers, then compared with the reference labels by ARI

Measures: the same statistic, rescaled against a random labelling
Settings: the null is a random labelling with the reference's cluster sizes held EXACTLY; corrected = (raw - null) / (1 - null), the adjustment ARI itself applies to the Rand index
Citation: Hennig 2007, with the ARI correction logic

Measures: the knee of the within-cluster sum-of-squares curve
Settings: maximum distance from the chord joining the first and last point of the min-max normalised curve over K = 2..10. A second, complementary heuristic - the discrete second difference - is in rfm_analysis.py and returns a different K on the same curve; both are shown in section 3 below
Citation: Thorndike 1953; Satopaa et al. 2011 for the chord form
